model_annotation: The chart is a grouped bar plot illustrating an “effect” measure across multiple language families, with six model/condition series shown side by side for each family and vertical error bars on every bar. The horizontal axis contains the categorical language-family groups (left to right: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, Uralic) and is labeled “family”; the vertical axis is labeled “effect” and uses a linear numeric scale with labeled ticks at approximately 0, 10, 20, and 30 (with the plotting range extending slightly below 0 and up to the mid-30s). For each family, six adjacent bars appear in a consistent color/legend order: XLM‑L₂ (light blue), mBERT‑L₂ (dark blue), mBERT‑R₂ (light green), XLM‑R₂ (dark green), mBERT‑B₂ (pink), and XLM‑B₂ (red). Approximate bar heights by family are: IE‑Baltic shows small positive effects (light blue ~2, dark blue ~1, light green ~3, dark green ~3–4, pink ~6, red ~5); IE‑Germanic shows mid-height light/dark blue bars (~9–10), near-zero to slightly negative green bars (light green ~0, dark green ~−1), and higher pink/red bars (~15 each); IE‑Indic shows near-zero light/dark blue (~0–1), taller green bars (light green ~20, dark green ~18), and the tallest pink/red bars in that group (pink ~24, red ~21); IE‑Romance shows moderate light/dark blue (~6–7 and ~4–5), light green around ~5 with dark green near ~1, a pink bar around ~12–13, and a red bar around ~6; IE‑Slavic shows light/dark blue around ~10–11 and ~9, near-zero greens (~0–1), and higher pink/red around ~17 and ~15–16; IE‑other shows light/dark blue around ~6 and ~5–6, greens near ~0, and pink/red around ~8; Isolate shows values clustered close to zero with small positives for the green and pink/red series (generally ~0 to ~2); Semitic shows larger light/dark blue (~11 and ~16), slightly negative greens (about ~−2 to ~−1), and larger pink/red (~15 and ~19–20); Uralic shows uniformly small positive values (roughly ~0 to ~2, with pink around ~1–2 and the others near ~0–1). Error bars are present for all bars, with several notably wide intervals (especially in Semitic and some IE groups), and the categories appear in a fixed family listing rather than being sorted by bar height; no individual bars are highlighted beyond the consistent color coding and the legend placed at the right of the plot.
